book_meta.subtitle_child: My First Ukrainian IPA Sound Book

ipa_key.name: Postalveolar Fricative
ipa_key.kid_desc: Lift your tongue near the bumpy roof of your mouth and blow a steady 'shhh' wind!
ipa_key.parent_desc: A voiceless postalveolar fricative /ʃ/, produced by channeling air through a narrow groove behind the alveolar ridge.

ipa_key.name: Tied Postalveolar Affricate
ipa_key.kid_desc: Tap the roof of your mouth to briefly catch the 'shhh' wind and pop it into a 'ch' sound!
ipa_key.parent_desc: The tie-bar above /t͡ʃ/ links /t/ (stop closure) and /ʃ/ (postalveolar release) into a single crisp affricate.

ipa_key.name: Close Back Rounded Vowel
ipa_key.kid_desc: Round your lips like a little fish and say a smooth, pure 'ooo'!
ipa_key.parent_desc: A pure close back rounded vowel /u/ without the English off-glide [ʊw].

ipa_key.name: Open Central-Back Vowel
ipa_key.kid_desc: Drop your jaw open wide and sing a clear, sunny 'aaah'!
ipa_key.parent_desc: An open unrounded vowel /a/, brighter than English 'father' and never reduced to schwa [ə] when unstressed.

sound_recipe.label: 1. Hushing Wind Channel
sound_recipe.detail: Start blowing a steady 'shhh' stream behind your top gum ridge.

sound_recipe.label: 2. Quick Tongue-Roof Seal
sound_recipe.detail: Without stopping your breath, tap your tongue blade up to briefly block the channel.

sound_recipe.label: 3. Crisp 'Ch' Release
sound_recipe.detail: Pop the seal right back open into a sharp 'ch' (like 'freSH CHeese')!

articulation.voicing: Voiceless throughout (vocal cords remain open and silent)
articulation.manner: Fricative /ʃ/ + Affricate /t͡ʃ/ Compound Cluster (Щ = Ш + Ч)
articulation.airflow: Oral, central fricative stream interrupted by brief stop closure and affricate release

word_breakdown.note: One Cyrillic letter representing two distinct postalveolar consonants pronounced smoothly together: /ʃ/ + /t͡ʃ/.
Lips round immediately during the release of /t͡ʃ/ into a pure, steady /u/.
Crisp, unaspirated voiceless velar stop /k/ (zero puff of air, unlike English initial 'k').
Retains full, clear open /a/ quality even in an unstressed final syllable.

mouth_placement_steps: Raise the flat blade of the tongue toward the postalveolar ridge (just behind the upper gum ridge) to form a narrow channel and begin a voiceless hushing '/ʃ/' ('sh').
Mid-stream, press the tongue blade firmly up against the postalveolar ridge to create the complete stop seal ('/t/') of the affricate without taking a new breath.
Release the tongue seal immediately back into the postalveolar groove to produce a crisp '/t͡ʃ/' ('ch'), fusing '/ʃ/' + '/t͡ʃ/' into one seamless gesture.

coaching_game.title: The 'Fresh Cheese' Bridge Game
coaching_game.setup: Write the English phrase 'freSH CHeese' on a card and underline the middle letters 'SH CH'.
coaching_game.action: Have your child say 'fre-SH CH-eese' slowly three times, then whisper the outer parts until only the middle '/ʃt͡ʃ/' bridge remains, and finally launch straight into 'щука' (/ʃt͡ʃuka/)!
coaching_game.success_cue: You should clearly hear BOTH the opening hush (/ʃ/) and the crisp tap-pop (/t͡ʃ/) inside the single letter Щ—never a single flat 'sh'!

common_pitfalls.issue: Pronouncing Щ as a Single Long Soft [ɕː] (Russian Interference)
common_pitfalls.fix: In Russian, Щ is a single long palatalized fricative [ɕː]. In Standard Ukrainian, Щ is always a hard two-part sequence /ʃt͡ʃ/ (Ш + Ч). Make sure the tongue makes a full stop contact (/t/) in the middle of the sound.

common_pitfalls.issue: Dropping the Internal Stop Closure and Saying Plain [ʃ]
common_pitfalls.fix: Young learners often simplify /ʃt͡ʃuka/ to [ʃuka]. Use the 'Fresh Cheese' cue so the child feels their tongue briefly tap the roof of the mouth to separate the opening /ʃ/ from the /t͡ʃ/ release.

common_pitfalls.issue: Aspirating the /k/ in the Second Syllable (/ka/)
common_pitfalls.fix: English speakers naturally add a breathy puff [kʰ] to 'k'. Keep Ukrainian к (/k/) completely unaspirated and crisp before the final open vowel /a/.
